summary: Set 119 Session 1 gives every verification finding a provenance and stops documentation wording from buying a metered review round. `evidencePaths` is now contract on BOTH verification surfaces: the markdown parse in `ai_router/verification.py` reads a tolerant `Evidence paths:` line, and `ai_router/pull_verifier.py` offers an ungated `evidencePaths` array on the `submit_verdict` tool, parsing it into `Finding.evidence_paths` and serializing it as `evidencePaths`. `normalize_evidence_path` strips the decoration reviewers actually write (backticks, emphasis, `./`, backslashes, `:<line>`, `#anchor`) so the same file compares equal across rounds. Both reviewer templates ask for it and call it mandatory on a Critical/Major finding; both artifact schemas declare it optional, deliberately, because its absence must not launder a blocking finding. On top of that contract sits the doc-only severity cap, applied at the one shared chokepoint `is_blocking_issue`: a finding whose cited paths are ALL documentation prose is recorded at Minor and opens no round, and `classify_blocking` reports the demoted findings in a new `doc_capped_issues` list and names the count in its reason so the cap is auditable rather than silent. The cap is an operator-attested verification reduction, journaled BEFORE any cap code was written (authority=human, rubric_line=verification-reduction, verification_effect=reduces), with the narrower Major-only alternative recorded as considered and rejected. Three properties keep it from being the anti-laundering rule in reverse: doc-ness is derived from paths and never self-declared; absence is not doc-ness (an uncited blocking finding is never cheaper); and behaviour-bearing markdown (`ai_router/prompt-templates/**`) is code that happens to be spelled in markdown. Shipped with exactly 30 test functions -- the spec's irony budget to the digit -- including the L-112-1 falsifier pairs that plant each rule both ways. Two changes the spec did not enumerate were required for correctness, not scope: `TEMPLATE_ID` moved `session-verification-v7` -> `v8` with a freshly computed pin, because the reviewer template is hash-pinned and an unbumped edit fails closed by design (16 integrity-gate tests said so); and `docs/path-aware-critique.schema.json` plus its pure-Python validator both learned the field, because a producer emitting a key its own artifact schema does not declare is exactly the L-066-1 drift. Cross-provider verification returned VERIFIED on round 1 from both discovery lenses, with two Minor nits recorded below.

reason.specifics: Session 2 builds `ai_router.close_preflight` against the same gate predicates this session's orchestrator has just read end to end (`gate_checks.py`, `run_of_record`, `close_backstop`, the verification stamp), and its step 4 replays history over `session-events.jsonl` -- the same ledger this session's evidence came from. Continuity of that context is worth more than provider diversity here, and cross-provider independence is preserved where it matters: verification still routes to a different effective provider. Session 2 also inherits two owed residuals from this session, both named in `ai-assignment.md` and in the nits below.

adjudicated_minor_nits.finding: Doc-capped findings are classified and reported as Minor/nit, but the raw finding dict preserves its original `severity` value, so a durable artifact may still read `Major` for a capped finding. (Discovery call 1, spec-conformance lens.)
adjudicated_minor_nits.rationale: Verification artifacts are RAW RECORDS and are never edited after they are written (session-constitution: `sN-issues*.json` is immutable). Rewriting a verifier's declared severity in the envelope would make the artifact say something the verifier did not say -- the same class of laundering the cap is guarded against, running through the writer instead of the classifier. The classification, not the stored label, is authoritative: every loop and gate consults `is_blocking_issue`, as the verifier itself observed. `classify_blocking.doc_capped_issues` exists precisely so a reader can see which findings were demoted without re-deriving it.

adjudicated_minor_nits.finding: `docs/path-aware-critique.schema.json` accepts a whitespace-only `evidencePaths` entry (a single space satisfies `minLength: 1`) while `ai_router/path_aware_critique.py` rejects it via `p.strip()`. A small schema/validator parity gap. (Discovery call 2, failure-scenario lens.)
adjudicated_minor_nits.rationale: Correct, and it is the L-066-1 class this repo names explicitly. It is Minor on consequence: the gap is FAIL-CLOSED (the Python validator is the stricter side, so nothing invalid is ever accepted at runtime), and the producer cannot emit the value -- `_coerce_evidence_paths` normalizes whitespace-only entries away before a `Finding` is built. The fix is one token: give the schema item the non-whitespace `pattern` that the sibling `description` property in the same file already carries. It is deliberately NOT applied in this session: the tree is frozen and stamped, and a post-verdict edit would stale `work_diff_sha256`, forcing a fresh routed backstop round to re-settle a one-character schema tightening. Session 2 already touches `ai_router/` and can fold it in before its own run of record.
